messages:
lina: Heads up — prepping Cloud KMS integration for the next wave of Private deployments. Need a quick checklist for service account bindings, key rings, and rotation. Anyone with notes?
sam: quick Q — are we doing envelope encryption (CMK wrapping DEKs) in customer project, or are we planning to pass keys to instances?
lina: envelope with CMK in the customer project. Our control plane will perform wrap/unwrap by impersonating a customer SA. We should avoid long-lived keys leaving the customer project.
raj: For impersonation flow the common pattern is: our control-plane SA gets `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the customer SA. The customer SA gets `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` (scoped to the cryptoKey). That lets us mint short-lived tokens and call KMS as the customer SA.
maria: agree. Recommend per-environment keyRings, and per-tenant cryptoKeys to make rotation and auditing easier. Also enable key versioning.
sam: note about GCP policy: serviceAccountTokenCreator is pretty powerful for that target SA but it's still better than adding our service account directly to every key ACL. Trade-off documented.
lina: can we put an example command and an IAM snippet here for the onboarding doc?
maria: sure — example bind (customer project side):
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding customer-project-123 \
  --member="serviceAccount:rp-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

# grant key encrypt/decrypt (scoped to specific key)
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/customer-project-123/locations/global/keyRings/prod-kr/cryptoKeys/app-dek \
  --member="serviceAccount:rp-control@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```
raj: Also ensure the customer enables Cloud Audit Logs for `cloudkms.googleapis.com` and export Admin/Data Access logs to a sink (BigQuery/Cloud Storage) we can reference in the security review. We need retention >= 365 days for compliance customers.
sec-bot: Reminder: enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud KMS (they are disabled by default for most projects). Export via `gcloud logging sinks create` and grant writer identity `roles/storage.objectCreator` / BigQuery writer role. :lock:
sam: rotation mechanics — set `--rotation-period` on the key and have a rewrap job: 1) create new key version 2) call KMS `encrypt` to rewrap any stored DEKs 3) mark old version as disabled and schedule destroy after grace period. Need idempotent tooling.
maria: For Private (customer VPC) where cross-project egress is disallowed, consider a lightweight kms-proxy inside customer network that holds the customer SA and performs KMS calls locally. We then call the proxy over mTLS with mutual auth. Reduces cross-project permission surface.
lina: Good point. Which approach do we recommend by default? Impersonation or proxy?
raj: Default = impersonation with tokenCreator (simpler onboarding). Proxy = opt-in for high-security customers or air-gapped setups. Document both patterns and the permission difference.
sam: action items: 1) terraform examples for both flows 2) permission checklist + least-privilege examples 3) rotation playbook (commands + cron job) 4) logging/export template and retention guidance. I'll draft TF snippets.
maria: I'll own audit export and a BigQuery schema for KMS audit events.
lina: I'll draft the playbook and onboarding doc; will include sample PR checklist for Customer Success to verify KMS bindings before go-live.
sec-bot: Automated note: open security checklist ticket required for Enterprise Private deploys. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/issues/987 (auto-created)
lina: thanks — tagging this for the runbook sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
